name: Kool G Rap
hook: A Corona, Queens rapper whose dense, multisyllabic crime narratives on 'Road to the Riches' (1989) are widely credited with starting mafioso rap.
blurb: Nathaniel Wilson, born in 1968, grew up in Corona, Queens, and connected with DJ Polo and producer Marley Marl through the Juice Crew. As Kool G Rap and DJ Polo, their 1989 album 'Road to the Riches', produced entirely by Marl, paired dense rhyme patterns, with many-syllable rhymes and rhymes inside the line packed into a single bar, with crime and gangster stories. That was years before the combination became its own style, mafioso rap, and the album is widely cited as where that style starts. His rhyme density is one of the most directly cited influences on the more elaborate rap styles of the 1990s.
